answer: Neighborhood Overlap Quorum. Each agent publishes its peer set; an identity counts only if its neighborhood overlaps a quorum of distinct neighbors' neighborhoods above a fixed threshold. The overlap graph's crystal structure means a fabricated cluster must mirror real adjacency, so isolated rings fail. Every new vertex an attacker adds must be separately woven into that adjacency, costing one maintained link per identity per epoch plus sustained traffic to keep overlap scores above threshold. A nebula of cheap disconnected identities scores near zero.
